Hypnosis can induce a temporary retrieval block (posthypnotic amnesia) where suggested material is inaccessible until a cancellation cue, indicating a mechanism by which hypnosis manipulates access to stored memories [d1]. However, multiple high-credibility sources report that hypnosis does not improve recall compared to normal methods and instead increases false memories and people’s confidence in them [d2, d4, d7, d8]. Professional bodies and research caution that techniques like hypnosis are more likely to distort memory than to enhance accurate recall [d3, d8]. A practitioner’s anecdotal report suggests a 50–80% chance of recovering lost memories, but acknowledges no guarantee and ongoing controversy around hypnosis’ validity [d5].
